images.filename: A nice boardwalk runs all round the island, along Lake Ontario (27287330444).jpg
images.caption: Paths run all along the island, along the shores of Lake Ontario. This pleasant wooden boardwalk with fallen foliage strewn it was another slice of heaven, with the huge expanse of Lake Ontario on one side. Only, as this is a lake and not the sea, there was no sound of the waves hitting the beach. Also, Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport is about 5 km north of here (straight ahead 5km away), and this being a rather busy commuter airport serving mostly turboprops, there was a constant hum of airplanes coming in to land. (Toronto, Canada, Nov.2015)
images.alt: Paths run all along the island, along the shores of Lake Ontario. images.filename: A colourful array of canoes on the banks of the inlet from Lake Ontario (27621372600).jpg
images.caption: A colourful array of canoes stacked upside down on the banks of an inlet which comes in from Lake Ontario (which is just beyond). The blue canoe at the far end bears the name of the club (Toronto Island Canoe Club). According to their website, Toronto Island Canoe Club is a non-profit organization dedicated to promoting the sport of sprint canoe/kayak and to providing opportunities for youth and adults to learn about water safety, develop small boat skills and enjoy the lagoons of Toronto Island. (Toronto, Canada, Nov.2015)
